title: Buy The Dip Market Mechanics - What Needs To Happen For A Proper Crash!
creator: Sven Carlin
summary: Sven Carlin explains the mechanics keeping the market rising and what would have to break for a proper crash. Filmed on Wednesday, before Thursday's sell-off, the video argues the rally is driven by flows, not fundamentals: passive investing is now 55-60% of market activity, with roughly $500bn of annual 401k/retail inflows, $1.6tn of foreign inflows into the US in 2025, and ~$800bn-1tn of buybacks. Under the inelastic market hypothesis (Gabaix & Koijen), each $1 of inflow lifts market capitalisation by $5-8, so ~$2tn of flows explains ~$10tn of gains. A real crash would need those flows to reverse: 401k contributions turning net negative (projected from 2028 as baby-boomer required distributions grow), foreigners pulling out of $20tn+ of US assets, buybacks stopping, and a recession severe enough to trigger panic selling. He cites Mark Spitznagle as still bullish, expecting no crash before 2027-28, and quotes Buffett on being prudent when others are not. For investing now he points to pockets of value rather than the expensive index: Realty Income (dividend, growth, inflation protection), Netflix (discussed two days earlier), Kaspi (high dividend yield) and very oversold China internet stocks. No explicit buy, hold or sell call is made on any single ticker; the video is a macro framework plus a value watchlist. Caption garbles: 'Spitzagle' for Spitznagle, 'gabik and coen' for Gabaix & Koijen.
